commits.message:
fix(contrast): at ansi, text is measured in the terminal's own sixteen colours (rich-contrast-knmh) (#264)

* fix(contrast): at ansi, text is measured in the terminal's own sixteen colours (rich-contrast-knmh)

ensureContrast, ensureDrawn and drawnColour measured a STANDARD-depth pair
on STANDARD_TABLE's nominal colours. The writer does pick the index by that
table, but the terminal draws the index in its theme's colour, and themes
disagree about sides: Rosé Pine Dawn's black is light and its white dark, so
navy on white passed at 16:1 nominal and drew at 2.1:1.

Each now takes a trailing `terminal: TerminalTheme` and measures in its
ansiColors; a replacement is the writer's colour for the index that clears
the floor there. With none named the table is the VGA sixteen that
DEFAULT_TERMINAL_THEME draws, so existing answers are unchanged.

* fix(contrast): a replacement is ranked on the author's colour; one owner for the unnamed terminal (rich-contrast-knmh)

Review of PR #264 (high):
- The replacement index was ranked by distance to the truecolor pre-pass,
  which slides toward the pole the nominal ground names. Under a terminal
  that draws the ground on the other side (Rose Pine Dawn) that pole is
  wrong. Ranking on fg itself measured closer to the author's colour at
  both ANSI and 256 colours across every bundled terminal.
- 'No terminal means VGA' had two homes (colorMath's STANDARD_TABLE
  fallback and getTruecolor's INTERNAL_DEFAULT_THEME); resolveTerminal is
  now the one.
- The depth-to-table map is one exhaustive switch, resolved once per call.
- docs/contrast.md says readableOn measures in VGA at STANDARD
  (rich-template-bindings-wrzr).

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(contrast): a TerminalTheme holds exactly the sixteen ANSI colours; translucent text is ranked over its own ground (rich-contrast-knmh, rich-color-qqkm)

Review of PR #264 (medium):
- At STANDARD an index picked from a terminal's ansiColors is read back from
  the sixteen-entry writer table, so a 256-entry ansiColors returned
  undefined typed as ColorRgba. Every reader already indexes the table 0-15
  and the class doc names it the theme's sixteen; the constructor now
  refuses anything else, and its header stops calling it a 16/256 LUT.
- The replacement ranked fg composited over the terminal's drawn ground,
  which under Rose Pine Dawn turns a translucent navy into lavender. It is
  the author's colour over the author's ground.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(contrast): measure through the writer's own downgrade; say inputs are written colours (rich-contrast-knmh)

Review of PR #264 (escalation high):
- shownAs measured via drawnTable's own match, a second account of the
  index the writer emits beside ColorSpec.downgrade + getTruecolor, the one
  Style.drawnColors writes. It now goes through that; the tables only list
  replacement candidates.
- docs/contrast.md: fg and bg are the colours written, not the terminal's
  shades; the example passes undefined for substrate instead of a hand copy
  of the writer's black.
- resolveTerminal's comment no longer claims the widgets' fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(contrast): the terminal example imports what it uses (rich-contrast-knmh)
